name: Free arms read on the current code
research_question: Do the free offline arms behind delegated tasks, exact changes, data kept in scope, engine reuse and the hub checks still pass on the current code, and should their rows be recorded so 83 percent of the quick weight stops reading as unmeasured?
reevaluate_condition: seven daily recordings from 2026-11-18 are in results.csv, or the platform owner reverses the 17 Nov approval
held_fixed: zero model calls;a row is recorded only on a clean committed tree;paid arms stay under the hold on repeated paid evaluations
in_scope: the eleven offline arms of the overall metric that cost nothing to run; the two cases that miss in each of the scope arms
outside_scope: paid arms; changing weights or the bar
learned: 2026-11-16, unrecorded, zero model calls: eight of the eleven arms run on the current code give the same counts as their stale rows (queued tasks 43 of 43, deep run contract 53 of 53, deep runner 11 of 11, decision sink 15 of 15, allowlist writer 15 of 15, bounded writer 20 of 20, conversation recall 9 of 10, recent context 9 of 10). No regression since the rows were recorded. Not yet run: the three engine reuse arms and the hub scan. 2026-11-16, later pass: the last five were read, zero model calls. Secret scanning 35 of 35 and examples 37 of 37, the hub scan 256 of 278 and the spend ablation 0 of 15 as before. The public surface arm read 54 of 78 where its stale row read 101 of 101: not a regression of the code, the cases still named module paths from before the move into the five containers (no consumer imports them). Nineteen cases now name the modules where the names live (the offline import of the command line module among them, restored after a release review found it removed though its module only moved), five whose subject was deleted are removed, and the arm reads 73 of 73; its row is recorded on the committed tree. Two known misses stay as they are: one paraphrase case each in conversation recall and recent context, which word matching cannot reach. 2026-11-17: the platform owner approved recording the free offline arms once a day for 7 days. 2026-11-18 (commit b15a3aeb) and 2026-11-19 (8cc6beb6, rows in a6d99ea2): eleven free arms recorded current at zero model calls; quick floor 0.811 both days, headline 0.974, full floor 0.545. The deep run contract (53 of 53) and deep runner (11 of 11) rows are among them, so neither is stale.
changed: 2026-11-16: public surface cases follow the moved modules (73 cases).
decision: record the free arms once a day through 2026-11-24 (approved 17 Nov); then decide whether daily recording becomes the standing rule, by whether a recording ever caught a change the stale rows hid

name: An empty read is not an answer of zero
research_question: How should a turn answer when the read it planned returns nothing, so that it reads the collection itself or says what it could not read instead of answering zero or unavailable?
held_fixed: cheap tiers;the fix is generic, never keyed to a case
in_scope: the most frequent failure cause of the real asks tested in the app (three asks on 2026-11-15)
learned: 2026-11-16: one cause found by reading the code path, zero model calls. In the app's code runner a read of a collection's entries by an id that names no collection of the person's returned an empty list and left no record, so the reviewer and the reply writer took a total built on it as the person's data. Fixed in the app's backend (commit fce58524 on its month branch): the system records such a read, tells the reviewer once how to correct it, and a turn that ends uncorrected says which records could not be read; an empty collection of the person's stays a fact. Three tests on the real runner, sandbox and database pass, with the 37 earlier coverage tests. Not yet shown: that this is the cause in the three real asks, because no live case was run (the hold on paid runs, and the dev model key is refused). A second possible cause stays open: entries were read and the program summed a field that does not exist.
decision: keep running: rerun the three real asks one at a time when the dev key works; if a zero remains, look at the summed field next

name: Sub-metrics for the ideals that have none
research_question: Which readings that are already recorded and free to read can serve as sub-metrics of the three ideals that hold 67 percent of the overall weight and have no sub-metric, so the floor can rise above one third?
held_fixed: weights per ideal in the balance table;recorded rows only, nothing re-recorded to move the number
in_scope: ideal-moves-me-forward, QI3 and QI4: one free reading each, built and tested offline first
learned: 2026-11-16: the premise was a reading error. Every ideal already has a sub-metric; the 67 percent came from a run that read one sub-metric of nine and took the ideal weights over that part alone, which also doubled the floor (0.016 shown, 0.008 on the whole metric, 8 percent of the weight measured). The weight that is unmeasured sits on eleven free offline arms whose rows are stale since early November.
